summary: This program asks for the current temperature and then advises whether you need a hat. It uses an if/else pair so that exactly one of the two messages is printed, no matter what number you type.

lines.text: input always hands back text, so float() converts what was typed into a decimal number that can be compared with 10. The result is stored in temp for the test on the next line.
This is the condition that decides everything: if the temperature is below 10 degrees, the indented block underneath runs.
The indentation is what ties this line to the if above it, making it the cold-weather advice.
The else branch covers every case the condition missed — here, 10 degrees or warmer — so the program always gives an answer.
This is the addition the exercise asks for, telling the reader when a hat is unnecessary rather than staying silent.
